placements.why: This envelope's whole content is a calibration report (instrument identity, calibration value, verification against a named reference standard) and nothing in the supplied strata or graph structure — both empty — covers organizational calibration work. Calibration is named in the org's own enumerated strata vocabulary but has not yet been minted in this repo's structure, so this envelope's content is the first real instance calling it into existence.
placements.title: Instrument calibration becomes a standing, verifiable organizational category
placements.frame: What instrument or system was calibrated, and against what named reference standard was that calibration verified?

placements.title: Instrument correctness is established by verification against an archived reference standard, not by assertion alone
placements.frame: Does this calibration claim rest on verification against a named, dated reference standard, and does that verification hold across the full range the instrument is claimed to cover?
placements.why: All three segments carry the same directional theme at different grains: src-1 states the calibration and its verification against June reference plates holding across the band; src-2 and src-3 restate the same evidentiary move in structured field-label form. No existing leaf can hold this (the graph is empty), and the grain test is satisfied — this is a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding (verification-against-standard as the ground of correctness), not a one-time fact. The frequency value and June plates are themselves the fact-level evidence supporting this theme, not leaves of their own.
